frontier.hypothesis: The ledger already contains ONE existence proof of a counted-then-combine-deleted out2 copy - rejected/s4-form-minus-banned-wrap-floor9.c reaches out2 5 refs / live 42 BYTE-FREE - and it has never been dumped. If the reason cse1 spared that single-use copy is a reproducible condition rather than mere adjacency to its use, the same condition at a ~20-insn def->use span yields 5 refs / live 59-67 = pri 1481-1666, inside the window, byte-free = match.
frontier.mechanism: an unidentified cse.c condition that blocks the copy propagation measured in every other position (candidates: the source qty invalidated between def and use, or the use sitting inside the call-argument setup sequence after invalidate_for_call), followed by combine.c deleting the producer post-flow.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_80041188/s5/idump.sh on that form and diff the loop2 region of its .cse and .combine against s5/va/* insn by insn to name the sparing condition; then try to reproduce that condition with the copy placed earlier in loop2.

frontier.hypothesis: The seats can be fixed WITHOUT any reference lift by changing the hard-reg CONFLICT set: if the pa4 carrier conflicted with hard reg 22 ($s6) the way every allocno here already conflicts with reg 16 ($s0), the carrier would take s7 at its existing pri 1473 and out2 would take s6 at 714 - target seating with the C otherwise unchanged.
frontier.mechanism: global.c global_conflicts / mark_reg_live records a hard-reg conflict for every hard reg live across an allocno's range, and find_reg excludes it in both passes (visible in the BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG 'conflicts:' lines).
frontier.next_probe: Establish WHAT makes reg 16 live across almost every allocno in this function (read .flow/.greg for hard-reg 16 ranges and the global_conflicts path), then decide whether any ORDINARY-C construct (register-asm pins are banned) can hold a live value in a callee-saved hard reg across the carrier's range.

frontier.hypothesis: The body shape itself is the obstacle: every chassis in the ledger assumes the merged 'stptr' (loop1 walker re-initialised as loop2's pointer), and no perturbation of it can supply a combine-deletable out2 mention. A different loop2-pointer structure derived from the target asm may supply one naturally.
frontier.mechanism: H-s6-5: target's three materialised s6 references plus the pure-priority seat rule force >= 4 flow-counted out2 references in the original, so the original source shape differs from ours somewhere that costs no bytes.
frontier.next_probe: Rederive in 'rederive' modality from target asm + m2c under the explicit constraint 'out2 has >= 4 flow refs and exactly 3 materialised ones', instead of perturbing the current body (the rule-era chassis warning applies: the committed shape was calibrated to 16 regfix rules and is not evidence of original structure).
